scenes.title: The Curious Cat Arrives
scenes.description: A sleek black cat with glowing yellow eyes pads into the backyard. It sniffs around Halloween decorations, tail high, completely unaware of what's about to happen.
scenes.prompt: Cinematic low tracking shot of a sleek black cat with glowing yellow eyes walking through a dark suburban backyard at night, Halloween decorations, spooky yet whimsical, filmic lighting, Grok Imagine style

scenes.title: Laser Battle Erupts + Skeleton Joins In
scenes.description: The snakes explode into action, firing cyan and magenta lasers. The plastic skeleton suddenly animates, grabs a fallen laser, and starts blasting back while doing a ridiculous skeleton dance.
scenes.prompt: Wild Halloween backyard battle: glowing snakes firing lasers, animated plastic skeleton dancing and shooting back, black cat watching in horror, neon chaos, cinematic, Grok Imagine style

scenes.title: Pizza Guy Appears (Deadpan Reveal)
scenes.description: The house porch lights flick on. A bored pizza delivery guy stands on the porch holding a pizza box, completely unfazed by the laser battle happening 20 feet away.
scenes.prompt: Photoreal cinematic film still, 16:9 medium shot from just inside the open screen door, framed from mid-thigh up, of a pizza delivery man in his late twenties in a clean, correctly worn, slightly faded red polyester delivery polo with a small embroidered patch too soft to read, a matching red cap worn straight, a plastic name tag turned edge-on so no letter can be read, dark work trousers with a sharp crease, scuffed black canvas sneakers, perfect upright posture that makes him the straightest vertical line in the frame, shoulders relaxed, chin level, half-lidded calm eyes and a professionally neutral face, the expression of a man reading a street number on his fourth stop of a normal shift, not brave, not scared, simply post-surprise. He stands centered on a worn painted-wood back porch, holding a cardboard pizza box perfectly level in both hands as if presenting a sacrament he does not believe in, a cheap smartphone lit in his breast pocket, a folded stack of extra napkins on the box lid. Behind him, twenty feet back and softened by depth of field but readable: two glowing serpents about three feet long with faintly iridescent scales and triangular heads, one lit from within in cyan and one in magenta, eyes glowing like something powered rather than born, firing solid beams of colored light from open jaws that scorch neat black lines into the grass, a plastic party-store skeleton mid two-step, a smoldering hay bale, and at the porch rail's far end the black cat, a sleek real short-coated black cat with yellow eyeshine, small at the edge of frame, sitting with her tail curled around her feet and watching with complete composure. Lighting is two worlds that never mix: a hard warm 2700K tungsten porch bulb and amber jack-o'-lantern flicker on one side, cool 4100K full-moon light and saturated cyan and magenta laser spill on the other, every wet blade of grass and every damp leaf carrying a two-color specular edge, a thin ground mist catching the beams. The caged bulb sits directly above him, throwing sharp downward shadows under the cap brim and the box; a weak blue fill from the TV behind camera touches the front of his polo. Camera: 50mm, chest height, f/2.8, focus on his eyes, background beams rendered as long soft cyan and magenta streaks. Micro-detail: polyester sheen and pilling at the collar, moths in the bulb cage, rain beads on the box, a maple leaf stuck to the doormat, peeling porch paint. Grade: filmic teal-and-tungsten, fine 35mm grain, gentle vignette. No text, no captions, no watermark, no signature, no readable logos or brand names, no legible house numbers or name tags, no extra or fused fingers, no extra limbs, no duplicated faces, no warped hands on props, no illustration, no cartoon, no 3D render look, no anime, no plastic airbrushed skin, no HDR halos, no oversharpening, no lens-flare spam, no modern smartphone UI unless stated.
